chapter: Moving, Columbia Missouri and leaving home
title: CCC work, playing piano in the mess hall
summary: The company cleared land, Thompson was thrown off a work truck, and the men loved him for playing piano in the mess hall.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: It was predominantly black company, yes.
How many men in it, around?

I don't remember, there could have been 500. And we were dealing in conservation of land, you know, clearing wooded lands. I think now perhaps this is how the present freeways started, by the clearing of those swamp lands. And I -- at one time I got so disgusted I wanted to get out with the boys, I got mad at all that clerical work, and I should have been crazy, I must have been crazy because it was so easy it wasn't even funny. The rest of the guys had to go out in the mud and everything, and so I got mad and I jumped on the truck one day with my fatigues and my canteen, and they threw me off the lake like they'd thrown me in the lake that time at the golf course.

As if to say get out of here buddy, go back in that office. Because -- well, not only that but they all loved me. This is really something that I would have to say, and I'm so happy, that the guys loved me. Because I played the piano in the mess hall, you know. In fact like I never had to worry about eating. You know how when the guys sit down to eat in the army, everybody sits down and you have to have what they call this boarding house reach. You
know, after they say the blessing and all, (noises). You know, I mean, and everything's gone.

If you don't have enough reach, it's like being an athlete or a basketball player, you really have to be like a basketball player. You have to reach way over there and get the bread, and get the butter and everything, and the milk is in the pitcher, you have to grab the pitcher. And you can just imagine -- and you can't spill it. You can't be a heathen. That's another thing about the army that's really great. It has discipline that is great for people, you know.
Now, imagine, all this is going on, and these guys are -- but nobody's spilling anything, because, you know, they don't allow it.
